title: Environment variable manifest
description: One row per distinct process.env.NAME read under apps/api/src, apps/api/scripts, packages, scripts. See config/env-manifest.yaml and archive/sessions/2026-09-02-t14-cheap-extras-plan.md.

purpose.description: What this variable is for, in plain English.

provider.description: The vendor/service this key belongs to, or the literal string 'internal' for platform-internal config (no external vendor).

holder.description: Who holds the real value. 'unknown' is allowed and must be listed in the handoff for Petter to fill in.

cost_class.description: 'none' for internal config with no external cost (flags, URLs, internal secrets).

required_in.description: Which contexts fail to boot/run correctly without this set. Empty means none: the variable is optional everywhere (feature off or fallback when unset).

set_in.description: Where the real value(s) actually live today. 'none' for a variable that is read but never actually configured anywhere (dead-but-not-yet-marked-retired candidate).

cost_note.description: Free-text vendor cost fact (tier, quota, price) — lets BUDGET.md point here instead of repeating numbers.

docs.description: Optional path or URL to more detail (a doc, a vendor console, an onboarding note).

example_value.description: Optional placeholder value used verbatim in generated .env.example files. Never a real credential.

retired.description: Calendar date this variable stopped being read, and the field that exempts a row from the dead-row check. For a variable that was never read but is deliberately retained anyway (a vendor key held against future use), the date this was recorded — say which in cost_note, because the two cases read identically here.

read_indirectly.description: True when code genuinely reads this variable but not via the literal `process.env.NAME` / `process.env["NAME"]` text the checker scans for (e.g. a typed wrapper that takes `process.env` as a parameter and destructures/accesses it inside). Exempts the row from the dead-row check. Use sparingly — verified by hand, not by the checker — and explain the real call site in `purpose` or `docs`.
